author: suman-bhatta
body:
This pull request sets up the foundational structure for a new Django project named `user_service`. It includes the initial configuration files, app setup, and boilerplate code required to get the project running.

### Project Initialization:

* Added `manage.py` to serve as the command-line utility for managing the Django project. This file allows for administrative tasks like running the server and managing migrations.
* Created the `settings.py` file with default configurations, including database setup (SQLite), installed apps, middleware, and other essential settings for the project.

### Core Configuration:

* Added `asgi.py` and `wsgi.py` for ASGI and WSGI configurations, respectively, enabling support for asynchronous and synchronous web servers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c9d3cfb5eeae99884185ddda27714e40daaa9e6aa74985ad00f9abf8d9dac00fR1-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bdd9505bfc30406887126c2b4e65eaad38350ac2671e858bc21dc8c8c4b3d80cR1-R16)
* Created `urls.py` to define the URL routing for the project, currently including only the admin interface.

### App Setup:

* Initialized a `users` app with boilerplate files (`admin.py`, `apps.py`, `models.py`, `tests.py`, `views.py`) to serve as the foundation for user-related functionality. These files are currently placeholders. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4376b4473ad6a8cd2b174dd68c1aa3015014af30981b7cf33a8d0226b5f26c48R1-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2145a230168b2e2ebe2a1a0d9671690b7623e127deab1561c0ce4cb8235e67e6R1-R6) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-07f6e3893ba0f5a83f52f5f7a21a4ee9c3d41f58d1ebcaa41492b47854be7e4cR1-R3) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-46f66bc732d7bed931c595717917feb77ee60888c28fbde6f440d031d1ad6c2cR1-R3) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-4e894ac82da19d1cc562ca6fffcd4bb92a502481b84357673c7a39815add3e7dR1-R3)

This PR classifies the assertion error saying that the start offset of Kafka source is greater than end offset to either user error or Kafka internal error. There are different possible cases that can lead to this error. Here is a list in the time order that we can catch them:
1. If the user specifies startingOffset and endingOffset in a comparable way (either by index or timestamp), we can compare them before starting the query.
2. If the user provides startingOffset and endingOffset but they are incomparable initially, we should compare them as soon as they are resolved by contacting the kafka brokers.
3. If the user sets startingOffset to some value and endingOffset to latest, we should compare them after the query has started and the latest offset has been fetched.
4. It is a Kafka topic-partition is broken.
```
java.lang.AssertionError: assertion failed: Beginning offset 49041276637 is after the ending offset 48774253518 for topic xxx partition 1. You either provided an invalid fromOffset, or the Kafka topic has been damaged

	at com.databricks.spark.util.ExecutorFrameProfiler$.record(ExecutorFrameProfiler.scala:110)
	at org.apache.spark.rdd.RDD.computeOrReadCheckpoint(RDD.scala:406) 
```

author: cobbledsteel
body:
Refactor decoder to build instruction maps from all executable sections in an ELF.

This is because different build flows follow varying ELF conventions. Chipyard/BaremetalIDE
flow creates one .text section for instructions, but others, e.g. Zephyr, can have multiple 
(text section, plus separate sections for reset logic, ISRs, etc).

Iterate through all sections in an ELF, and use SectionFlags to check if the section is marked
as executable. Aggregate instructions from all relevant sections and put them in a hashmap.
Instead of using entrypoint when extracting instructions, set entrypoint to be the start of the
currently processed section.

Additionally, StackUnwinders also needs to search for symbols. Also update symbol search
logic to iterate through all relevant sections.

First take on a contributing guide for `ty`. Lots of it is copied from the existing Ruff contribution guide.

I've put this in Ruff repo, since I think a contributing guide belongs where the code is. I also updated the Ruff contributing guide to link to the `ty` one.

Once this is merged, we can also add a link from the `CONTRIBUTING.md` in ty repo (which focuses on making contributions to things that are actually in the ty repo), to this guide.

Feel free to update/modify/merge this PR before I'm awake tomorrow.

body:
## Features
- [X] record patterns `{ident:p, ...}`
- [X] implements pattern conjunction (&) in the ucs
- [X] implements pattern disjunction (|) in the ucs

## Implementation
Both operators are implemented as syntactic sugar for sequentialization or new splits :
```
if e is
  p | q then sequel
  alternatives
```
is transformed into
```
if e is
  p then sequel
  q then sequel
  alternatives
```
in the same way
```
if e is
  p & q then sequel
  alternatives
```
is transformed into
```
if e is
  p then if e is
    q then sequel
    alternatives
  alternatives
```

## Possible improvements
- [ ] propagate more thouroughly information that a scrutinee is an object to avoid the runtime checks repetition

Potential fix for [https://github.com/tommichael88/booktomnyc/security/code-scanning/38](https://github.com/tommichael88/booktomnyc/security/code-scanning/38)

To fix the issue, we should avoid using `innerHTML` to insert untrusted data into the DOM. Instead, we can use `textContent` to safely insert the `selectedItem` value as plain text. This ensures that any special characters in the `selectedItem` value are escaped and cannot be interpreted as HTML or JavaScript. Additionally, we can create the button and its child elements programmatically using DOM methods to avoid any reliance on HTML strings.


_Suggested fixes powered by Copilot Autofix. Review carefully before merging._

This PR fixes #3036 TTL Znode doesn't expire in Test envs

### Description

- [x] Here are some details about my PR, including screenshots of any UI changes:

(Write a concise description including what, why, how)
The issue is related to ZooKeeper's TTL (Time-To-Live) node functionality and specifically how it behaves in the embedded ZooKeeper environment used in tests.

In a normal ZooKeeper deployment, a background ContainerManager thread runs periodically to clean up expired TTL nodes. However, in the embedded ZooKeeper used for testing, this background thread doesn't appear to be functioning properly. The ContainerManager is designed to run on a configurable schedule (default is 60 seconds), but in the test environment, this cleanup process doesn't happen.

The way we solve it is by creating a custom ContainerManager and using a fakeElapsedTimer.

author: rc-zb
body:
Add [万象拼音基础版](https://github.com/amzxyz/rime_wanxiang) as rime-wanxiang. This is a feature-rich pinyin schema for the Rime input method framework.

The schema requires to work the grammar model `wanxiang-lts-zh-hans.gram`. However, this file is [released](https://github.com/amzxyz/RIME-LMDG/releases/tag/LTS) by carelessly overriding the old versions (see amzxyz/RIME-LMDG#22), which makes it impossible to reproduce over time. So I decide just not to include it, and prompt the user to download it themselves.

## 🛠️ 작업 요약

*   **멘토링 상태 변경 기능 추가**: 멘토링 세션의 상태(`MentoringStatus`)를 업데이트할 수 있는 API를 구현했습니다. 이 기능은 상태 변경을 요청한 사용자가 해당 세션의 멘토 또는 멘티인지 확인하는 권한 검증 로직을 포함합니다.
*   **`more-details` API (`my-matches`) 상태 필터링 기능 추가**: 특정 멘티의 프로필에서 신청한 멘토링 세션 목록을 조회할 때, `status` 파라미터를 통해 진행 상태별(`IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED` 등) 필터링 기능을 추가했습니다. 이는 사용자가 언급하신 "신청한 매칭 더보기 필터링"에 해당합니다.

## 📝 작업 상세

### 멘토링 상태 변경 기능 구현

*   **API**: `POST /v1/matching/status`
*   **기능**: 요청 본문으로 전달받은 `mentoringId`에 해당하는 멘토링 세션의 `status` 값을 요청된 `MentoringStatus`로 변경하고 저장합니다.
*   **요청**: `MentoringStatusUpdateDTO` (멘토링 세션 ID, 변경할 멘토링 상태)를 사용합니다.
*   **권한 검증**: 상태 변경을 시도하는 현재 로그인 사용자가 해당 멘토링 세션의 `menteeId` 또는 `mentorId`와 동일한지 확인합니다. 권한이 없는 경우 `AccessDeniedException`이 발생합니다.

### `more-details` API (`my-matches`) 상태 필터링 기능 구현

*   **API**: `GET /v1/user/profile/{nickname}/more-details`
*   **기능**: `type=my-matches` 요청 시, 선택적인 `status` 쿼리 파라미터를 받아 해당 상태의 멘토링 세션 목록만 페이징하여 반환합니다. `status` 파라미터가 없을 경우 모든 상태의 세션을 조회합니다.
*   **구현**:
    *   `ProfileController`의 `getMoreDetails` 메소드에 `@RequestParam(value = "status", required = false, defaultValue = "ALL") String status` 파라미터를 추가했습니다.
    *   `MenteeProfileService`의 `getMyMatchesPaged` 메소드가 `status` 값을 받아 필터링 로직을 수행하도록 수정했습니다.
    *   `MentoringRepository`에 `findByMenteeUserIdAndStatusPaged` 쿼리 메소드를 추가하여 멘티 ID와 상태로 필터링된 페이징 조회를 지원합니다. 기존 `findByMenteeUserIdPaged` 쿼리에는 `ORDER BY m.createdAt DESC`를 추가했습니다.

## ✅ 체크리스트

- [x] 코드 점검 완료
- [x] 테스트 통과
- [x] 문서/주석 최신화

## 📚 기타

- 멘티와 멘토 모두 해당 멘토링의 상태를 변경할 수 있도록 구현하였습니다.

author: inclyc
body:
This is a lightweight CLI frontend for `nixf`, which provides fancy interface prompts in the terminal indicating whether Nix files contain errors (linter + syntax checker). In the discussion at https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/332695, we talked about how `nixf-tidy` needs a good user interface to display errors, and this package fulfills that requirement while also aiming to promote the adoption of linter checks within `nixpkgs`.

### Usage Instructions:

Assume you have a Nix file with nits:

```nix
/* /tmp/a.nix */
rec {
  a = 1;
  b = 2
}
```

Run the following command:

```
> nixf-diagnose /tmp/a.nix
```

```
Error: expected ;
   ╭─[/tmp/a.nix:4:8]
   │
 4 │   b = 2
   ·        │ 
   ·        ╰─ expected ;
───╯
Warning: attrset is not necessary to be `rec`ursive
   ╭─[/tmp/a.nix:2:1]
   │
 2 │ rec {
   · ─┬─  
   ·  ╰─── attrset is not necessary to be `rec`ursive
───╯
```

For more description, see https://github.com/inclyc/nixf-diagnose

### Binary / Closure size?

There is no need to pull the entire `nixd` as a dependency. If you only use the `nixf-diagnose` executable, it occupies approximately 2.2 MiB of disk space. Specifically:

- This executable: 1.5 Mib
- nixf library: 754.45 Kib

author: jakujobi
body:
This commit modifies the assembly test files (test75.asm, test81.asm, test82.asm, test83.asm, test84.asm, test85.asm, test86.asm, test87.asm) to enhance procedure calls and variable handling. Key changes include:

- Corrected the procedure call in test75.asm by replacing the placeholder error identifier with the actual procedure name.
- Introduced new assembly test files (test81.asm, test82.asm, test83.asm, test84.asm, test85.asm, test86.asm, test87.asm) implementing various procedures with improved variable assignments and arithmetic operations.
- Ensured consistency in loading and storing values using the base pointer (BP) across all updated files.

These modifications contribute to a more robust and maintainable ASM generation process, building upon previous enhancements.

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive automation script for deploying and monitoring a lightweight Kubernetes (K3s) cluster with Azure Arc and Grafana. The changes include new documentation, Bicep templates, and modules for infrastructure setup, monitoring configuration, and deployment. Below are the most important changes, grouped by theme:

### Documentation and Overview
* Added a new Jumpstart guide in `script_automation/arc_k8s_monitor_grafana/_index.md` that provides detailed instructions for setting up a K3s cluster, onboarding it to Azure Arc, and using Grafana with Azure Monitor Dashboards for monitoring. Includes prerequisites, architecture diagrams, deployment steps, and dashboard usage instructions.

### Infrastructure Deployment
* Added `main.bicep` template to define parameters and modules for deploying the required Azure resources, such as virtual networks, subnets, and Azure Monitor Workspace. Includes support for optional Azure Bastion deployment.
* Added `main.bicepparam` parameter file to configure deployment options, such as SSH keys and Bastion deployment.

### K3s Cluster Deployment
* Added `modules/k3s.bicep` module to deploy a K3s cluster on an Azure VM, configure SSH access, and install monitoring scripts for integration with Azure Monitor and Prometheus.

### Management Artifacts
* Added `modules/mgmtArtifacts.bicep` module to set up supporting infrastructure, including virtual networks, subnets, network security groups, and Azure Monitor Workspace. Supports optional Azure Bastion deployment for secure access.

Describe your pull request here ---- Please read the [guidelines for Bioconda recipes](https://bioconda.github.io/contributor/guidelines.html) before opening a pull request (PR). ### General instructions * If this PR adds or updates a recipe, use "Add" or "Update" appropriately as the first word in its title. * New recipes not directly relevant to the biological sciences need to be submitted to the [conda-forge channel](https://conda-forge.org/docs/) instead of Bioconda. * PRs require reviews prior to being merged. Once your PR is passing tests and ready to be merged, please issue the `@BiocondaBot please add label` command. * Please post questions [on Gitter](https://gitter.im/bioconda/Lobby) or ping `@bioconda/core` in a comment. ### Instructions for avoiding API, ABI, and CLI breakage issues Conda is able to record and lock (a.k.a. pin) dependency versions used at build time of other recipes. This way, one can avoid that expectations of a downstream recipe with regards to API, ABI, or CLI are violated by later changes in the recipe. If not already present in the meta.yaml, make sure to specify `run_exports` (see [here](https://bioconda.github.io/contributor/linting.html#missing-run-exports) for the rationale and comprehensive explanation). Add a `run_exports` section like this: ```yaml build: run_exports: - ... ``` with `...` being one of: | Case | run_exports statement | | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | semantic versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x") }}` | | semantic versioning (0.x.x) | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` | | known breakage in minor versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | known breakage in patch versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | calendar versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin=None) }}` | while replacing `"myrecipe"` with either `name` if a `name|lower` variable is defined in your recipe or with the lowercase name of the package in quotes. ### Bot commands for PR management
Please use the following BiocondaBot commands: Everyone has access to the following BiocondaBot commands, which can be given in a comment:
@BiocondaBot please update Merge the master branch into a PR.
@BiocondaBot please add label Add the please review & merge label.
@BiocondaBot please fetch artifacts Post links to CI-built packages/containers.
You can use this to test packages locally.
Note that the @BiocondaBot please merge command is now depreciated. Please just squash and merge instead. Also, the bot watches for comments from non-members that include `@bioconda/` and will automatically re-post them to notify the addressed ``.

body:
## Problem
At present, deleting any block above a `Text` block causes a crash. This is because (**note**: i'm guessing here as i'm not 100% confident) the blocks re-rendered and the new state is immediately fed to `JSONForms` via `FormBuilder` prior to the update loop being complete.

Closes [insert issue #]

## Solution
Shift the update for block state **below** the state update for drawer, so that `FormBuilder` doesn't see the new state whilst its internal state hasn't been updated.

## Tests 
- [ ] Navigate into any page
- [ ] Add any **non text** block
- [ ] Add a text block
- [ ] Verify that the text block is **below** the first block
- [ ] Attempt to delete the firste block

author: ronan-fesselier
body:
Good day,

This commit reverts Test_Gmod_Properties from using LINQ's MaxBy to a manual loop.
The previous MaxBy implementation did not correctly select the lexicographically largest code when multiple Gmod nodes shared the same maximum code length.

For example, if GMOD data contained both "C1053.3112" and "C1053.3114" with the same maximum code length, and ".3112" was encountered first during iteration, MaxBy would select ".3112".

The new manual loop, with its explicit lexicographical comparison for ties, correctly selects the lexicographically larger ".3114".

Consequently, the ExpectedMaxes dictionary has been updated to reflect the correct maximum codes from the json based on this refined logic.

Thanks,

body: ## Description The Prometheus alerts ConfigMap uses several metrics that have been deprecated in kube-state-metrics v2. According to the [kube-state-metrics deprecation documentation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/blob/release-1.9/docs/README.md#metrics-deprecation), This PR updates our metrics to use the new format. ## Changes Updated the Prometheus alerts ConfigMap to replace all instances of deprecated metrics with their newer equivalents: - kube_pod_container_resource_requests_cpu_cores → kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu",unit="core"} - kube_pod_container_resource_requests_memory_bytes → kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory",unit="byte"} - kube_node_status_capacity_pods → kube_node_status_capacity{resource="pods",unit="integer"} - kube_node_status_allocatable_cpu_cores → kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu",unit="core"} - kube_node_status_allocatable_memory_bytes → kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="memory",unit="byte"} ## Related Issues Related astronomer/issues#6193 ## Testing ### Tested the new metric formats by running the queries on prometheus - `kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu",unit="core"}` - `kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory",unit="byte"}` ### Tested that old metrics queries are not coming up on prometheus ### Tested that recording rules are returning values - `namespace:kube_pod_container_resource_requests_cpu_cores:sum` - `namespace:kube_pod_container_resource_requests_memory_bytes:sum` ## Merging 1.0

author: 0gonge
body:
## 🚘 What kind of work?

<!-- PR에 대한 전반적인 설명을 적어주세요. -->
Wispy에서 주로 쓰일 primaryButton 컴포넌트를 구현했습니다. 
Color, Font를 전역적으로 사용할 수 있도록 세팅했습니다. 

## ✈️ Changes

<!-- 작업 내용을 리스트로 작성해주세요. -->

- PrimaryButton 컴포넌트 구현 - 배경색은 고정되어있습니다! 

- 텍스트 색상(textColor)과 외부 스타일(style, textStyle)을 props로 유연하게 조절 가능하도록 구현했습니다. 
- fontFamily적용해주었습니다.
- 안드로이드에 ripple 효과 적용 (android_ripple)
- iOS에서도 pressed 상태 시 opacity 효과 적용
- fonts.js를 통해 모든 SUIT 폰트 정의 및 fontAssets로 분리
- App.js에서 useFonts(fontAssets)로 폰트 로딩 관리
- AppLoading으로 폰트 로딩 전 화면 처리
- App.js에서 일단, GreetingScreen을 기본 렌더링해서 버튼과 폰트 확인했습니다. 
## 🎡 Thoughts

<!-- 깊이 고민한 내용을 작성해주세요. -->
- Expo에서 커스텀 폰트를 적용할 때 useFonts()를 사용할 수 있지만, 여러 개의 폰트를 적용할 경우 App.js에 일일히 등록해야 했습니다.
 = 이를 fonts.js에 Fonts와 fontAssets로 분리하여 관리함으로써 유지보수에 용이하도록 했습니다.
- 어린이 사용자 대상 앱이기 때문에 버튼 인터랙션 피드백을 시각적으로 확실하게 주는 것이 UX 관점에서 중요하다고 판단했습니다. 그렇기에 버튼 컴포넌트에 ripple 효과, pressed 효과를 추가했습니다.

## 🚥 Screenshot

<!-- 작업한 화면이 있다면 스크린 샷으로 첨부해주세요. -->

| iOS | 
| --- | 
|![IMG_7681](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e75086a-d7c1-4b90-a0d8-8e39bb63a870)| 

## 🚖 To Reviewers

<!-- 리뷰어에게 주목했으면 하는 점 or 바라는 점을 적어주세요. -->
사용법입니다! 
## Colors
```js
import Colors from '../constants/colors';

<Text style={{ color: Colors.wispyBlue }}>
  Hello, I'm wispy!
</Text>
```

## Fonts
```js
import Fonts from '../constants/fonts';

<Text style={{ fontFamily: Fonts.suitHeavy, fontSize: 18 }}>
  Hello, I'm wispy!
</Text>
```

## PrimaryButton
```js
import PrimaryButton from '../components/PrimaryButton';

<PrimaryButton onPress={() => console.log('pressed')}>
  Next
</PrimaryButton>

<PrimaryButton
  onPress={handlePress}
  textColor="#ffffff"
>
  Next
</PrimaryButton>
```
이렇게 사용할 때 import 해주고, 눌렸을 때 handlePress에 기능 구현해주고, 
textColor와 Text를 받아서 유동적으로 사용해주시면 됩니다! 

ps. iOS는 작동 잘 되는 거 확인했습니다. 안드로이드 시뮬레이터에서 폰트 적용 잘 되는지 실제 기기에서 테스트 한 번 부탁드립니다!

참고 :
https://reactnative.dev/docs/style
https://github.com/facebook/react-native/blob/main/packages/react-native/Libraries/Components/Button.js

body:
This is essentially the same as #940 but I've created a separate PR because the other branch was too behind the main and a rebase was creating a few unwanted commits for some reason.

The two main changes here are:

1. Since the distance matrix is symmetric, the inner loop limits were changed to avoid going through the same matrix elements more than once
2. `@floop` was replaces by `Threads.@threads`. Not sure why, but a simple banchmark using Chairmarks showed that it actually works (in the dfigure below, the first benchmark was done using `@loops` and the second using `Threads.@threads`):
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85a262ca-14a9-45bc-adf0-300f589fcb95)

author: ansengarvin
body:
As I discussed in #52, it was getting extremely unwieldy to create and pass states and drill them into my various props. I've implemented Redux stores for four categories: Graphics settings, Universe settings, Debug Info and UI controls. All useStates() in these categories have been refactored to use selectors and dispatch as needed. The only major multi-component state that remains is leaderboards - I'm not sure what category I would put that in, but it may be good to move it into some sort of a redux store anyway.

I've also throttled the use of dispatch and setState within the animation frame rendering to about 20 every second. Previously, it was one every frame. I believe this will reduce some overhead and improve performance, and the number can be easily adjusted if I need to throttle it more.

I also did some work leading up to a UI refactor. The tab setup I have wrapping the leaderboard has been separated into its own component, and I'd like to re-use it to separate settings out into different tabs.

Finally, the camera issue mentioned in #48 was fixed up when I moved those controls over to redux.

・名前・年齢・職業・自己紹介の情報を入力し、送信ボタンを押すとバリデーションを行い、JSON形式で送信データをコンソールに表示するアプリを作成しました。
・名前・年齢・職業・自己紹介の情報入力欄をそれぞれ項目を選ぶ形や、長文がかけるテキストボックスなどの形で実装しました。
・バリデーションチェックにて、未入力や不正な形式があればそれぞれエラーメッセージが表示されるよう実装しました。
![スクリーンショット 2025-05-13 150140](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8606042-86d7-4311-b43a-494263c0a109)
![スクリーンショット 2025-05-13 150118](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccf27158-2dff-4d7f-8ac6-da5090e0b3b8)

【APIからデータを取得して表示】
・ダミーAPIからユーザー一覧を取得し、ページにリスト表示するアプリを作成しました。
・情報が取れなかった際はアラートが出るように実装しました。
**・読み込み中の表示（例：読み込み中...）を出すという要件を見落としておりました…（すぐに実装いたします）**
![スクリーンショット 2025-05-13 150149](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d49021a8-bdc5-4bc2-b871-7c9c55083972)

## 🧠 自己評価（必ず記入）

| 評価観点                        | 自己評価（1〜5） | 理由・根拠 |
|---------------------------------|------------------|------------|
| テーマの目的を理解しているか     |         4         |       今回の演習で一番の肝であるfetchを使ってAPIと連携してレスポンスを処理するコードが全く想像できないところからのスタートであったため、基礎的な知識のインプットをするところから始めました。結果、フォームの構造やfetchに関しての基本は理解できたかなと感じています。     |
| コードが目的に沿って書かれているか |          5        |      無駄なコードは書かないよう心掛けながら実装に取り組みました。また、難しいコードを使うのではなくできるだけ簡潔に、わかりやすいコードを書くことを心掛けました。      |
| 評価観点に沿った取り組みができたか |         2        |      今回、いつものように評価観点をノートにメモすることを行わなかったため、一つ要件を見逃してしましました。周りからだいぶ遅れをとっていると感じて焦っていたことや、インデントの確認に気を取られていたことから起きたことであると感じるため、今後は提出する前に全ての事柄に対しての確認を怠らないよう心掛けます。      |
| 自走して実装できたか             |           4       |       フォーム、APIに関して全く知識がなかったため、自分から積極的に学ぶ姿勢をもって取り組むことができました。     |

### **PR Type** Enhancement, Documentation, Other ___ ### **Description** - Major backend refactor introducing persistent chat history with MongoDB, JWT authentication, and robust AI chat/image analysis endpoints. - Added a new Gemini-powered flashcard generator API with PDF upload and comprehensive documentation. - Implemented new and improved Mongoose models for chat sessions and history. - Enhanced StudyHub frontend with a redesigned StudyHome page, new interactive calendar (FullCalendar integration), and improved AI chat with image upload and persistent history. - Improved cart removal logic, error handling, and user feedback in the marketplace. - Updated navigation, icons, and routing for a more cohesive user experience. - Added and updated multiple CSS files for better responsiveness, visual polish, and new UI sections. - Added and updated package.json and .env files for new features, dependencies, and configuration. - Deleted numerous unused or redundant node_modules files to clean up the repository. ___ ### **Changes walkthrough** 📝
Relevant files
Enhancement
21 files
index.js
Major refactor: MongoDB chat history, image upload, and robust AI chat
API
chatbot-chat/index.js
  • Refactored to use ES modules and modern imports (dotenv, express,
    cors, multer, MongoDB, GoogleGenerativeAI, session, cookie-parser,
    path).
  • Added MongoDB integration for persistent conversation history per
    user.
  • Enhanced chat endpoint to support both text and image (file upload)
    inputs, with improved error handling and model selection.

    check endpoint.

    image analysis.

    generation via file upload.

    parsing.

author: codchen
body:
## Describe your changes and provide context
An EVM transaction may take "snapshots" during its execution, which is implemented as branching out another layer of cachekv under sei's store structure. During normal chain execution, these branched cachekvs will be flushed to the base cachekv/context at the end of a transaction. However during `traceBlock` calls, such flushing doesn't happen, and subsequent transaction's "base" context is its predecessor's multilayer cached context. Although this would not cause correctness issue, it may make certain store operations (e.g. iterator) slow. This PR makes sure any outstanding contexts are flushed to the base context before tracer starts on each transaction.

## Testing performed to validate your change

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
# Add clear error messages for RPC endpoint connection failures

## Description
This PR addresses issue #240 by adding clear error messages when RPC endpoint connections fail. Previously, when an RPC connection failed, the system would panic with a nil pointer dereference without clearly indicating that the RPC connection had failed.

Changes made:
1. Added proper error handling in `RegisterToAVS` function to check for errors from `RegisterOperatorWithAvs`
2. Improved error messages in `NewOperatorFromConfig` to clearly indicate when RPC endpoint connections fail
3. Added more descriptive error messages that include the RPC URL in the error message

## Testing
The changes have been tested by verifying that the error messages are properly propagated when RPC connections fail.

## Link to Devin run
https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6814af2d51cb48c287909cfa1e68c09a

## Requested by
Chris Li (chris@avaprotocol.org)

Fixes #240

author: watson
body:
### What does this PR do?

This fixes a few race conditions in the logic related to adding and removing breakpoints:
    
- If there's no active debug session and two probes are being added at the same time, the 2nd of the two might try to attach it self to the session before the first probe has had a chance to start it.
- When removing the last probe, the debug session is stopped. But if another probe is being added while the session is being stopped, the session might not be started up again.
- When adding a new probe while there’s only a single existing probe and that existing probe is also being removed, the breakpoint logic might think it’s the last probe and disable the debugger.

### Additional Notes

There's a lot of whitespace changes in this PR. Enable "Hide whitespace" for an easier review experience 😃

author: mmmarcos
body:
Related to #8422

Changes in this PR:

- Added extra info about app in `snapcraft.yaml` and `package.json`.
- Added instructions on how to build snap locally
- Moved desktop entry to a specific file in the `assets` directory. The following keys were changed:
  - Added `SingleMainWindow=true` so that the desktop manager does not include a "New Window" action
  - Added `StartupNotify=false` to be explicit that this is not managed
  - Added `StartupWMClass=parsec` to be explicit about the wmclass
  - Fixed `Categories` to use `;` separator
  - Added `Keywords` to make it easier to find the application
  - Added `GenericName` and improve `Comment`

See: https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/recognized-keys.html

author: kaikozlov
body:
**Fixes #77, #105, and #111**

Hi!

This pull request addresses a performance degradation issue where touchpad scrolling and gestures become laggy over extended use.

**Problem:**
This pull request addresses the issue where MiddleClick causes progressively worsening trackpad lag (scrolling, gestures) over time. This often becomes noticeable after sleep/wake cycles or display reconfigurations, requiring an application restart to restore performance.

The root cause is a resource leak related to how the `CGEventTap`'s `CFMachPort` was managed within the `RunLoop`:

1.  `CGEvent.tapCreate` returns a `CFMachPort`.
2.  The previous code added this port directly to the `RunLoop` (`RunLoop.current.add(...)`). Internally, `CFRunLoop` creates a `CFRunLoopSource` wrapper to monitor this port.
3.  The cleanup code attempted to remove the original `CFMachPort` (`RunLoop.current.remove(...)`), which failed because the run loop manages the *wrapper source*, not the original port directly.
4.  This resulted in **orphaned `CFRunLoopSource` objects** remaining active every time listeners were re-registered (e.g., after sleep/wake).
5.  These accumulating sources consumed resources and interfered with the input event stream, causing the progressive lag.

**Solution:**
This PR modifies `Controller+Mouse.swift` to manage the run loop source explicitly and correctly using CoreFoundation APIs:

1.  An explicit `CFRunLoopSource` is now created for the event tap's port using `CFMachPortCreateRunLoopSource`.
2.  This *specific source* is added to the run loop via `CFRunLoopAddSource`.
3.  During cleanup, `CFRunLoopRemoveSource` removes the *exact source* that was added.
4.  `CFMachPortInvalidate` is called on the port during cleanup to explicitly release system resources and break potential cycles.
5.  Additional validation checks (`CFMachPortIsValid`) have been integrated into the registration and cleanup logic for increased robustness against potentially invalid tap states.

**Testing:**
I've tested this fix locally over the past week. The touchpad performance remains consistently smooth, and the previous lag issue is no longer reproducible. The core three-finger tap functionality remains unaffected.

**Impact:**
This change significantly improves the application's stability and user experience for long sessions by preventing resource leaks that caused system-wide input lag. It directly fixes the reported performance degradation without altering the application's primary features.

body:
Cut over a few things to be backed with DQLite state in the client application facade.

In particular, cut over our calls to EndpointBindings to a new service method.

This required a small change to the state method getEndpointBindings. In the DDL for application_endpoint and application_extra_endpoint, a NULL value in space_uuid represents the endpoint is bound to the application's default space. We now fill in this default value in the return value

This _could_ cause trouble to modelmigration, however, we have a check in the import code to ensure we don't fill in the space_uuid if it's the same as the application's default space. I have added some more tests for this case.

$ juju bootstrap lxd lxd
$ juju add-model m
$ juju deploy juju-qa-test
$ juju show-application juju-qa-test

  base: ubuntu@20.04
  principal: true
  exposed: false
  remote: false
  life: alive
  endpoint-bindings:
    "": alpha
    info: alpha
    juju-info: alpha

Snyk has created this PR to upgrade mongodb from 6.15.0 to 6.16.0.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.
- The recommended version is **13 versions** ahead of your current version. - The recommended version was released **22 days ago**.
Release notes
Package name: mongodb
  • 6.16.0 - 2025-04-21

    6.16.0 (2025-04-21)

    The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 6.16.0 of the mongodb package!

    Release Notes

    distinct commands now support an index hint

    The Collection.distinct() method now supports an optional hint, which can be used to tell the server which index to use for the command:

    // providing an index description
await collection.distinct('my-key', { 
  hint: { 'my-key': 1 }
});

// providing an index name
await collection.distinct('my-key', { 
  hint: 'my-key'
});

    This requires server 7.1+.

    Driver support for servers <=4.0 deprecated

    Warning

    Node driver support for server 4.0 will be removed in an upcoming minor release. Reference: MongoDB Software Lifecycle Schedules.

    Fix processing of multiple messages within one network data chunk

    During elections, or other scenarios where the server is pushing multiple topology updates to the driver in a short period of time, a bug in the driver's socket code led to backlog of topology updates that would remain in the buffer until another heartbeat arrived from the server. This could lead to delays in the driver recovering from an election and/or an increase in MongoServerSelectionErrors.

    Now, all messages in the current buffer are returned to the driver leading to faster processing times.

    Huge thank you to @ andreim-brd for sharing a self-contained reproduction that proved to be instrumental in the identification of the underlying issue!

    FindCursor.rewind() throws documents?.clear() is not a function errors in certain scenarios

    In certain scenarios where limit and batchSize are both set on a FindCursor, an internal driver optimization intended to prevent unnecessary requests to the server when the driver knows the cursor is exhausted would prevent the cursor from being rewound. This issue has been resolved.

    Features

    • NODE-6494: add support for hint on distinct commands (#4487) (40d0e87)
    • NODE-6515: deprecate driver support for server 4.0 (#4517) (4c1a8a7)

    Bug Fixes

    • NODE-6630: read all messages in buffer when chunk arrives (#4512) (8c86e30)
    • NODE-6878: documents.clear() throws a TypeError after cursor is rewound (#4488) (a1fffeb)

    Documentation

    • Reference
    • API
    • Changelog

    We invite you to try the mongodb library immediately, and report any issues to the NODE project.

body:
using the SyncFileService for the save / load of all XElement objects. 

this means we can add settings so we ignore invalid charecters for xml as part of the save and load. 
so in rare circumstances things with escape characters in them will still save and load as part of uSync. 

it does mean these files might not be strictly valid xml and fail to parse in other tools but they will work as text files and as part of the sync.

This PR updates the full-list error screen to be adaptable for when the keyboard is shown.

body:
The PR add missing MKL functions from VM namespace to the dedicated extension:
- `arg()` to be used by `dpnp.angle`
- `copysign()`
- `i0()`
- `inv()` to be used by `dpnp.reciprocal`

Note, `remainder()` is available as MKL VM function but follows C's module operator and so can't be used to implement `dpnp.remainder` which has to follow Python's module operator according to Python array API [specification](https://data-apis.org/array-api/2024.12/API_specification/generated/array_api.remainder.html):
> This function is equivalent to the Python modulus operator x1_i % x2_i.

Note, `sycl::half` is not intended to be used for VM functions due to accuracy reason and values mismatch with numpy in corner cases.

Define the initial specification to be used for the 'exact' scheme for the Sui Blockchain.

This specification is designed to be optimally flexible for clients to be able to fully leverage PTBs (Programmable Transaction Blocks) to either provide a direct payment or perform a set of operations to swap from one asset to the asset expected by the resource server. It also provides the optionality for leveraging sponsorship/gas-less transactions.

Per the contribution guidelines this only includes a proposed specification and after its been accepted and merged we can work on providing an implementation of the spec.

author: eddykasp
body:
The approximator uses multiple fixed sizes to set sizes for top-down layout according to the number of nodes in a graph. It also lays out two hierarchy levels in one step to keep them at the same scale.

The LAYOUT_NEXT_LEVEL approximator lays out the given graph and sets its algorithm to fixed layout. This allows laying out multiple hierarchy levels in one pass to essentially combine bottom-up and top-down layout.

A new interface ITopdownLayoutApproximator is introduced allowing size approximators to be defined for specific layout algorithms.

author: sebastianpiresmolin
body:
This pull request refactors the `FactoryController` and `MqttClientWrapper` classes to improve JSON handling and MQTT integration. It replaces the previous nested map structure with `nlohmann::json` for better flexibility and adds functionality to publish sensor data snapshots to an MQTT topic. Additionally, it updates the test suite to align with the new structure and functionality.

### Refactoring for JSON Handling:
* Replaced `std::unordered_map<std::string, std::unordered_map<std::string, double>>` with `nlohmann::json` in the `FactoryController::getSensorStates()` method to provide a more flexible and structured representation of sensor data, including machine state. (`include/FactoryController.h` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f4c9466c40ffb10d32550929eb5181c0c20fd55ed4ed86cf9d2eed242789c37aL16-R19) `src/FactoryController.cpp` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f2206140f4d6d9cc56f91d822fb645a3bd1a01a79202e2356e43e8d0ce27d462L51-R61)
* Updated the `FactoryController` and related files to include the `nlohmann/json.hpp` header for JSON support. (`include/FactoryController.h` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f4c9466c40ffb10d32550929eb5181c0c20fd55ed4ed86cf9d2eed242789c37aR8-R9) `src/FactoryController.cpp` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f2206140f4d6d9cc56f91d822fb645a3bd1a01a79202e2356e43e8d0ce27d462R4)

### MQTT Integration Enhancements:
* Added a new method `MqttClientWrapper::publishSensorData()` to publish JSON-formatted sensor data snapshots to an MQTT topic. (`include/MqttClientWrapper.h` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-222502d1235098865d129f1d88f9d203c328081e9569710cff36842fe6fdbc6dR19-R20) `src/MqttClientWrapper.cpp` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f26f380fe2e8e58944bbdc005040b65ff94235a12aafad7dad2383a58c0c90b4L24-R35)
* Modified `MqttClientWrapper::message_arrived()` to retrieve sensor snapshots from the `FactoryController` and publish them to the `factory/state_snapshot` topic. (`src/MqttClientWrapper.cpp` [src/MqttClientWrapper.cppL24-R35](diffhunk://#diff-f26f380fe2e8e58944bbdc005040b65ff94235a12aafad7dad2383a58c0c90b4L24-R35))

### Test Suite Updates:
* Removed outdated test cases for malformed topics and machine message handling, as these are no longer relevant with the new structure. (`tests/FactoryControllerTest.cpp` [tests/FactoryControllerTest.cppL10-R47](diffhunk://#diff-97ad5f1cae3f9ba01ecd3e6b19d274b113d93ecfe391189cb86fa6c7bc5252e5L10-R47))
* Enhanced the test case for sensor state snapshots to validate the new JSON structure, including machine state and multiple sensor values. (`tests/FactoryControllerTest.cpp` [tests/FactoryControllerTest.cppL10-R47](diffhunk://#diff-97ad5f1cae3f9ba01ecd3e6b19d274b113d93ecfe391189cb86fa6c7bc5252e5L10-R47))

This silences mypy type warnings and formatting errors that snuck in while the checks were disabled. body:
# Description

## Summary
This PR implements highly requested camera sensitivity controls for third-person view, allowing players to independently adjust horizontal and vertical mouse sensitivity. It also adds optional pitch limits to restrict how far up/down the camera can look.

## Motivation
Many users requested the ability to reduce vertical camera sensitivity independently from horizontal sensitivity, and some wanted to limit the camera's vertical range to prevent disorienting extreme angles.

## Changes

### Features
- ✨ **Independent camera sensitivity controls**
  - Separate pitch (vertical) and yaw (horizontal) sensitivity multipliers
  - Configurable through new `[CameraSensitivity]` INI section
  - Default: OFF - 100% vertical, 100% horizontal sensitivity

- ✨ **Vertical pitch limits** *(WIP - See Known Issues)*
  - Optional min/max angle restrictions
  - Prevents camera from looking too far up/down
  - Smooth clamping at limit boundaries

- ✨ **Debug mode for input troubleshooting**
  - Logs raw input values and transformations
  - Helps users tune sensitivity settings

### Technical Improvements
- 🏗️ Refactored game structures into separate header file
- 🔒 Added thread-safe player entity tracking
- 📐 Fixed camera angle calculations (degrees vs radians)
- 📝 Updated configuration system with new options

### Bug Fixes
- 🐛 Fixed erratic camera movement at pitch limits
- 🐛 Corrected input scaling for smooth camera control
- 🐛 Resolved degree/radian conversion issues

## Configuration
New INI settings:
```ini

; ===== CAMERA SENSITIVITY SETTINGS =====
[CameraSensitivity]
; Vertical (pitch) sensitivity multiplier
; Lower values reduce vertical (Up/Down) sensitivity (0.0-2.0)
; Example: 0.4 (40% of sensitivity)
; Default: 1.0 (100% - no change)
PitchSensitivity = 1.0

; Horizontal (yaw) sensitivity multiplier
; Lower values reduce horizontal (Left/Right) sensitivity (0.0-2.0)
; Default: 1.0 (100% - no change)
YawSensitivity = 1.0

; Enable pitch angle limits (true/false)
; When enabled, restricts how far up/down you can look
; Default: false
EnablePitchLimits = false

; Minimum pitch angle in degrees (negative = looking down)
; Only used when EnablePitchLimits is true
; Example: -180.0 degrees
PitchMin = -180.0

; Maximum pitch angle in degrees (positive = looking up)
; Only used when EnablePitchLimits is true
; Example: 180.0 degrees
PitchMax = 180.0
```

## Known Issues
- ⚠️ **`EnablePitchLimits` is experimental and not recommended for general use**
  - The TPV camera angle aligns with the last FPV state when switching views
  - This makes the pitch limits work incorrectly as they don't account for the initial head tracking state
  - The feature is included for testing but disabled by default
  - Will require additional research into the game's head tracking system


## Breaking Changes
None - all new features are optional and backward compatible.

## Additional Notes
This implementation uses the game's native input system to ensure smooth integration. The debug mode can help users find their preferred sensitivity settings.

author: braydonk
body:
On Linux, the context switch counts in the `status` file for a particular process only contain the context switches for that particular thread (the values taken directly from the [`task_struct`](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.14.6/source/include/linux/sched.h#L1105-L1106) for the process).

This means that in the current implementation, `NumCtxSwitches` can only give you the number of context switches for the main thread, and none of the subthreads (since on Linux `ProcessesWithContext` ends up using `d.Readdirnames` which ends up using `getdents` and thus does not show task IDs).

This PR adds a new `Process` method that will sum the voluntary and involuntary context switches from each status file in `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>`.

body:
A common need when using this library is to automatically select the user's country based on their IP or location. Since that's out of scope for this library (there's no reliable way to detect the user's country on the client side alone), I put together a [simple template](https://croct.com/templates/interface/form/react-phone-number-input) that integrates it with an external service.

The template uses [Croct](https://croct.com/), which offers a free-forever plan and makes it super easy to detect the user’s country from their IP. We've been using it in all our contact forms, and it’s been super helpful for improving UX by pre-filling the country field automatically.

I also added a new section to the README with a one-line setup and usage example:
```bash
npx croct@latest use npm://react-phone-number-input
```

Here's what it looks like in action:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d12e5c1b-f93e-49c5-a2c0-da382885c084)

Hope this helps others who’ve run into the same need!

#### Description

This change introduces a new `System::LayerImplDispatch` implementation for Darwin platforms.
It separates dispatch-based event handling from the socket-based `LayerImplSelect`, allowing better compatibility and readability when using `Network.framework`, which does not rely on POSIX sockets or select().

### Why
- The Network.framework backend doesn’t use file descriptors or select(), making `LayerImplSocket` a poor fit.
- Makes the code more maintainable and readable

### Changes
- Added `SystemLayerImplDispatch.h/mm` and `SystemLayerImplDispatchSockets.mm`
- Updated the system layer selection logic in GN  to route correctly when `CHIP_SYSTEM_CONFIG_USE_DISPATCH` is set
- Updated tests (TestSystemTimer, TestSystemWakeEvent, etc.) to support dispatch-based execution
- Cleaned up `SystemLayerImplSelect` by removing dispatch-specific logic that no longer belongs there

### Language and Survey Management
* Added support for multilingual surveys by introducing the `SurveyLanguage` and `LanguageDetail` models, along with a helper method (`getLanguageCode`) to manage language selection in surveys (`Survey.swift`, `SurveyManager.swift`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-28ce94d492677fc7a9da101150898332d1977d11ed504906a2bf79acff367f29R8-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-28ce94d492677fc7a9da101150898332d1977d11ed504906a2bf79acff367f29R39-L20) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f15df4851352e3c8871c2f41be5825227bdc59c5fc26f78c808bda6fd803bb33R65-R76) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f15df4851352e3c8871c2f41be5825227bdc59c5fc26f78c808bda6fd803bb33R253-R293)
* Enhanced survey filtering to handle multilingual surveys, ensuring surveys unavailable in the selected language are skipped with appropriate logging (`SurveyManager.swift`).

### Environment Configuration and Models
* Refactored `FormbricksEnvironment` to use an `internal enum` with computed properties for safer and more structured access to environment configuration, replacing static variables (`FormbricksEnvironment.swift`).
* Introduced a new `Segment` model with detailed filtering capabilities, including recursive filters, connectors, and operators, to support advanced segmentation logic (`Segment.swift`).

### Structural and API Updates
* Added a new property `recaptchaSiteKey` to the `EnvironmentData` model to support reCAPTCHA integration (`EnvironmentData.swift`).
* Updated the `UserManager` to include cleanup logic for `syncTimer` during logout, ensuring proper resource deallocation (`UserManager.swift`).

### Versioning and Access Modifiers
* Bumped the SDK version from `1.0.1` to `1.1.0` in the `FormbricksSDK.podspec` file to reflect the new features and changes.
* Adjusted access modifiers for several classes and enums to align with their intended scope, such as making `FormbricksAPIErrorType` and `Error` extensions public (`Error+Message.swift`, `APIError.swift`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e10cabac2c62882c9500e3d6a548ba1ece6cf36d05f4c76803860198ab078f7fL3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bc268c1e2601a2ba83143a16f3a52c593ee5fa604aded45669f97596940c50f6L3-R3)

Fixes #496.

This reads forces from a TRR trajectory, converts them from `kJ / (mol * nm)` to `kJ / (mol * Angstrom)`, and stores them in the atomic property `force`.
When writing, the conversion is done in reverse. For atoms without the atomic property set, a default value of zero force is written (should there be an error / warning?).

Additionally, some smaller changes:
- update Readme to reflect changes from #480.
- fix comparison in an C example.
- run `clang-format` and ICWYU on the TRR related files.

body:
# Recipe Integration and Forum View Enhancements

## Summary
This PR implements two significant improvements to the forum functionality:

1. **Recipe Integration**: Added the ability for users to create and view detailed recipes with nutritional information
2. **Forum View Enhancement**: Fixed issues with post author display in the forum view

## Recipe Integration Details

### New Features
- Users can now select "Recipe" as a post type when creating a forum post
- Recipe creation includes:
  - Searchable ingredient selection with amounts
  - Cooking instructions input
  - Automatic nutritional calculation (protein, fat, carbs, calories)
- Recipe display in post detail view with:
  - Visual nutritional information cards
  - Ingredient list with nutritional breakdown
  - Step-by-step cooking instructions

### Implementation
- Created new interfaces in `apiClient.ts`
- Added API endpoints for recipe operations:

- Enhanced `CreatePost.tsx` with recipe-specific UI:
  - Food search functionality
  - Ingredient selection and management
  - Recipe instruction input
  - Two-step submission process (post creation followed by recipe creation)

- Updated `PostDetail.tsx` to fetch and display recipe data:

## Forum View Enhancement

### Issue Fixed
Fixed an issue where post authors weren't properly displayed in the forum view due to inconsistent data structures from the API.

### Implementation
- Added code to handle both string and object formats for the post author:
- Applied consistent normalization across all data fetching operations:
  - Initial post loading
  - Pagination
  - Search results

## Technical Details
- Recipe-related components use existing food catalog API for ingredient selection
- Recipe UI includes dynamic nutritional information calculated from selected ingredients
- Recipe data is fetched only when a post has the `has_recipe` flag set to true
- Forum view handles edge cases like missing author data gracefully

## Testing
- Verified recipe creation workflow from start to finish
- Confirmed nutritional calculations match backend values
- Ensured post authors display correctly throughout the application
- Tested edge cases for both recipe and author display functionality

closes #276 .

body:
# Why

<!--
-->

On some Android devices, when the app is sent to the background during an active recording session, an error is thrown.
This breaks the recording flow and causes the recorded video to be lost.

# How

<!--
-->
Handled VideoRecordEvent.Finalize.ERROR_SOURCE_INACTIVE as a non-fatal error by adding it to the list of ignored errors.
This allows the recording to finalize gracefully and return the video instead of failing.

# Test Plan

<!--
-->
Manually verified on affected Android devices by backgrounding the app mid-recording and confirming the video is returned successfully.

author: baohg1508
body:
## Changes

- Added more log for performance
- Move ```await this.processBlockQueue();``` out of ```processHistorical``` condition

## Important

- [processBlockQueue] Replace ```processNewHead``` logic with ```processHistoricalBlocks```. The reason is that ```processNewHead``` updates the cursor and  ```processBlockQueue``` runs in parallel with ```onNewHeads```, which can lead to a race condition where ```processQueue``` updates the cursor after ```onNewHeads``` has already updated it (since anything in blockQueue can be considered as historical block because it's old so might as well use ```processHistoricalBlocks``` to process the whole queue in batch)

author: joaogw
body:
# Major System Integration: AI Itinerary, Location Access, and UI Refinements

## Description

This pull request introduces significant architectural and functional upgrades to the app, including integration with OpenAI's GPT-3.5 Turbo, system-wide geolocation capabilities, UI/UX fixes, route separation, component creation, and several bug/security fixes. It is a collaborative effort between João Pedro and Lucas Kenji.

## Main Changes

- [x] AI Integration (GPT-3.5 Turbo)
- [x] Geolocation System
- [x] UI/UX Improvements
- [x] Navigation Logic Enhancements
- [x] Component Creation
- [x] Security Fixes
- [x] SDK Upgrade
- [x] Documentation Update

## Details of the Changes

### 🔐 Authentication & Routing

- Created route separation system for authenticated and non-authenticated flows.
- Navbar is now hidden on the login screen and displays only on authenticated pages.
- Login button now successfully navigates to the Home page.
- Improved variable handling to avoid leaking `.env` values to GitHub.

### 📍 Location System

- Implemented system-wide device location access request.
- Location data is now globally accessible across the app.
- Introduced `Toast` component to alert developers when location requests are made on an emulator.
- Location shown on `CurrentStatusBar` now includes neighborhood and city name.
- Improved error messages for emulator usage.
- Map displays real-time location using latitude and longitude.

### 🤖 AI Integration

- Initial integration with **GPT-3.5 Turbo**.
- Prompt engine created with:
  - Static fallback prompts for testing
  - Temperature configured to `0.7` for more creative and human-like responses
  - Token considerations for detailed itinerary responses
- API request system built to generate itineraries using dynamic user parameters.
- Created new page to **display AI-generated itineraries**, including:
  - Navbar
  - Screen title
  - Mandatory OpenAI watermark
  - Area to render dynamic responses

### 🧭 UI / UX Refinements

- Fully restructured the **Home Screen layout**.
- All content on the Home Screen now scrolls together.
- Reworked **Generate Itinerary** button and `CurrentStatusBar` dimensions for better spacing.
- CurrentStatusBar now sits closer to the top while respecting Safe Area.
- Replaced coordinate display with user-friendly location names.
- Navbar top border corrected to avoid redundant edges.
- Improved navbar page highlighting for the *Generate Itinerary* screen.
- Updated text on Home Screen to be inclusive to all gender identities and improved typography.

### ⚙️ Component and Screen Creation

- Created **User Preferences page**, allowing users to select behavior and interests.
- Fixed duplication bug where behavior lists were nested.
- Enhanced layout and button interaction:
  - Titles aligned correctly
  - Scroll indicators removed
  - Border-radius preserved on selection
- Created reusable `Toast` component for developer alerts

### 🧪 Fixes & Patches

- Resolved `image-size` DoS vulnerability (closes issue #9 )
- Fixed issue #19 : Preference screen list nesting and layout issues
- Fixed login screen language inconsistencies
- Fixed wrong navbar current page display (closes issue #13  )

### 📦 SDK & Documentation

- Upgraded **Expo SDK to v53.0**
- Updated `README.md` with additional contributor details (LinkedIn, email, etc.)

## Related Issues

- Closed #9 
- Closed #13 
- Closed #19 

## Contributors

- João Pedro – AI Integration, Location System, UI/UX Rework, Preferences Page
- Lucas Kenji – Login Fixes, Preferences Page Interface, Security Patches

## How to Test

1. Run on a **physical device** for full geolocation access.
2. Log in from the **Login Screen** and verify the flow to Home.
3. Allow location access and verify location data shown on Home and map.
4. Navigate to the **Itinerary Page**, click Generate, and validate GPT-3.5 Turbo responses.
5. Open the **User Preferences** screen and interact with selection buttons.
6. Observe Navbar behavior across routes and test highlighting.
7. Confirm absence of `.env` variables in committed files.
8. Run the app with an emulator and confirm that a toast appears with proper messaging.

## Checklist

- [x] Functional login routing
- [x] Global geolocation system
- [x] AI prompt engine using GPT-3.5 Turbo
- [x] Preferences page fully working
- [x] Navbar visuals and behavior fixed
- [x] Home screen scroll integration
- [x] Emulator toast message present
- [x] Updated Expo SDK to v53
- [x] `.env` vars removed from source and public view. Now it's access is restricted like it should be
- [x] Documentation updated

body:
This pr won't be merged in current state. As we discussed in Zulip giving that much control over sun color/position to UI may have some consequences. E.g. too many "fancy" clownlike presets shared via UI mods and then showed on streams, that may scare away new players and also upset mapmakers. So best thing we can do is make 4-5 presets (early morning, noontime, sunset, cloudy weather etc.) hardcoded in engine and then let user to switch between them.

For now all functions are available in UI, so we can find best values for presets which looks ok on common maps (like Setons, Gap etc). Ui functions:
```Python
    SetTerrainLightingMultiplier(float)  #Default value is usually 1.5-1.6
    
    SetSunColorRGB(r, g, b)
    
    SetSunPositionXYZ(x, y, z)         #Description below
```

![изображение](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb9904bc-c348-4ce3-bbf5-93aa47b5e247)


Some examples on seton:

author: ottenhoff
body:
Students with late exceptions could not properly start a timed assessment after due date. When a student with extended time attempted to start after the regular due date, they would get stuck with a "Work is being saved" message until auto-submission.

This fix:
1. Adds logic to detect late exception cases when students start assessments
2. Properly respects extended due dates when checking if time has expired
3. Prevents auto-submission for students with valid late exceptions

body:
This pull request introduces a new GitHub Actions workflow to generate SLSA Level 3 provenance files for supply chain security. The workflow integrates with the OpenSSF's SLSA framework and includes steps for building artifacts, generating provenance subjects, and signing the provenance.

### New GitHub Actions Workflow for SLSA Provenance Generation:

* **Workflow Purpose**: Adds a new workflow, `generator-generic-ossf-slsa3-publish.yml`, to generate SLSA Level 3 provenance files, improving supply chain security. The workflow is aligned with the OpenSSF's SLSA framework and supports provenance verification.
* **Key Features**:
  - Triggers on `workflow_dispatch` and `release` events.
  - Builds artifacts and generates provenance subjects with SHA-256 hashes.
  - Uses the `slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator` action to sign and optionally upload provenance files as release assets.

author: kavanase
body:
This is a minor addition to https://github.com/materialsproject/pymatgen/pull/4400.

I found that there were some cases where an energy adjustment of `UFloat(0, 0)` were already present in `ComputedEntry.energy_adjustments`, avoiding the updated handling of setting `std_dev` to `np.nan` when it is 0 (and avoiding the `UFloat` warning about `std_dev` being 0).
When accessing the MP database and pulling ozonide structures (for which the MP Anion Correction is set to 0, with std_dev 0), it throws the `UFloat` warning again.

MWE:
```python
from pymatgen.ext.matproj import MPRester

with MPRester() as mpr:
    entries = mpr.get_entries_in_chemsys("Na-O")

for entry in entries:
    print(entry.name, entry.energy_adjustments)
```
where one of the outputs is:
```
NaO3 [CompositionEnergyAdjustment(name='MP2020 anion correction (ozonide)', value=0.0, uncertainty=0.0, description='Composition-based energy adjustment', generated_by='MaterialsProject2020Compatibility')]
```

The updated handling in this minor fix avoids the `UFloat` warning being unnecessarily triggered for these cases.

author: germanjablo
body:
I think it's easier to review this PR commit by commit, so I'll explain it this way:

## Commits
1. [parallelize eslint script (still showing logs results in serial)](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/c9ac49c12d1e0990c11dfe0964957c2f842883c1):
Previously, `--concurrency 1` was added to the script to make the logs more readable. However, turborepo has an option specifically for these use cases: `--log-order=grouped` runs the tasks in parallel but outputs them serially. As a result, the lint script is now significantly faster.
2. [run pnpm lint:fix](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/9c128c276ace129ff83c273167e26f9090b4af34)
The auto-fix was run, which resolved some eslint errors that were slipped in due to the use of `no-verify`. Most of these were `perfectionist` fixes (property ordering) and the removal of unnecessary assertions. Starting with this PR, this won't happen again in the future, as we'll be verifying the linter in every PR across the entire codebase (see commit 7).
3. [fix eslint non-autofixable errors](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/700f412a3348a15d4c2ec8c636a378a269b4f1e3)
All manual errors have been resolved except for the configuration errors addressed in commit 5. Most were React compiler violations, which have been disabled and commented out "TODO" for now. There's also an unused `use no memo` and a couple of `require` errors.
4. [move react-compiler linter to eslint-config package](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/4f7cb4d63a84be69b2131888bcc090ee04109310)
To simplify the eslint configuration. My concern was that there would be a performance regression when used in non-react related packages, but none was experienced. This is probably because it only runs on .tsx files.
5. [remove redundant eslint config files and fix allowDefaultProject](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/a94347995a70a0970598dcc73638de4f6f7ca289)
The main feature introduced by `typescript-eslint` v8 was `projectService`, which automatically searches each file for the closest `tsconfig`, greatly simplifying configuration in monorepos ([source](https://typescript-eslint.io/blog/announcing-typescript-eslint-v8#project-service)).
Once I moved `projectService` to `packages/eslint-config`, all the other configuration files could be easily removed.
I confirmed that pnpm lint still works on individual packages.
The other important change was that the pending eslint errors from commits 2 and 3 were resolved. That is, some files were giving the error: "[File] was not found by the project service. Consider either including it in the tsconfig.json or including it in allowDefaultProject." Below I copy the explanatory comment I left in the code:
```ts
// This is necessary because `tsconfig.base.json` defines `"rootDir": "${configDir}/src"`,
// And the following files aren't in src because they aren't transpiled.
// This is typescript-eslint's way of adding files that aren't included in tsconfig.
// See: https://typescript-eslint.io/troubleshooting/typed-linting/#i-get-errors-telling-me--was-not-found-by-the-project-service-consider-either-including-it-in-the-tsconfigjson-or-including-it-in-allowdefaultproject
// The best practice is to have a tsconfig.json that covers ALL files and is used for
// typechecking (with noEmit), and a `tsconfig.build.json` that is used for the build
// (or alternatively, swc, tsup or tsdown). That's what we should ideally do, in which case
// this hardcoded list wouldn't be necessary. Note that these files don't currently go
// through ts, only through eslint.
```

6. [Differentiate errors from warnings in VScode ESLint Rules](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/5914d2f48d00e6d3c9d02ec30e189e87d6071754)
There's no reason to do that. If an eslint rule isn't an error, it should be disabled or converted to a warning.
7. [Disable skip lint, and lint over the entire repo now that it's faster](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/e4b28f136008020235a2ad176242484b3cebf814)
The GitHub action linted only the files that had changed in the PR. While this seems like a good idea, once exceptions were introduced with [skip lint], they opened the door to propagating more and more errors. Often, the linter was skipped, not because someone introduced new errors, but because they were trying to avoid those that had already crept in, sometimes accidentally introducing new ones.
On the other hand, `pnpm lint` now runs in parallel (commit 1), so it's not that slow. Additionally, it runs in parallel with other GitHub actions like e2e tests, which take much longer, so it can't represent a bottleneck in CI.
8. [fix lint in next package](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/4506595f916dee368a0a052d4256640f5832f621)
Small fix missing from commit 5
9. [Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into fix-eslint](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/563d4909c13116b17e70e95d3dae9c3446c4cdb5)
10. [add again eslint.config.js in payload package](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/12401/commits/78f6ffcae78c8caa5e87e4b36a0d6d1d0bddd65a)
The comment in the code explains it. Basically, after the merge from main, the payload package runs out of memory when linting, probably because it grew in recent PRs. That package will sooner or later collapse for our tooling, so we may have to split it. It's already too big.

## Future Actions
- Resolve React compiler violations, as mentioned in commit 3.
- Decouple the `tsconfig` used for typechecking and build across the entire monorepo (as explained in point 5) to ensure ts coverage even for files that aren't transpiled (such as scripts).
- Remove the few remaining `eslint.config.js`. I had to leave the `richtext-lexical` and `next` ones for now. They could be moved to the root config and scoped to their packages, as we do for example with `templates/vercel-postgres/**`. However, I couldn't get it to work, I don't know why.
- Make eslint in the test folder usable. Not only are we not linting `test` in CI, but now the `pnpm eslint .` command is so large that my computer freezes. If each suite were its own package, this would be solved, and dynamic codegen + git hooks to modify tsconfig.base.json wouldn't be necessary ([related](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/11984)).

author: brainbolt
body:
These changes add two helpers for running automated tests as part of a build script: **MSpec** and **NUnit**.  
These helpers provide a consistent interface for executing tests and integrating results into the build process.

### Overview

Each helper exposes a `RunTests` method with the following signature:

```csharp
void RunTests(
    string[] assemblies,
    string outputDirectory,
    string options = "",
    bool continueOnFailedTest = false
)
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **assemblies** | An array of assembly file paths to test. |
| **outputDirectory** | Directory where the test result XML files will be written. |
| **options** | A string of additional options to pass to the NUnit or MSpec runner. See [NUnit Options](https://docs.nunit.org/articles/nunit/running-tests/Console-Command-Line.html) and [MSpec Options](https://github.com/machine/machine.specifications/wiki/Command-line#console-runner) for details|
| **continueOnFailedTest** | Determines whether the build should continue if any test fails (`true`), or stop immediately on failure (`false`). |

### Behavior

- When `continueOnFailedTest` is `false`, the build will stop if any test fails.
- Test results are written to the specified `outputDirectory` as XML files.  
- A summary of the results (number of tests run, passed, and failed) is printed to the build output.

author: faern
body:
My main aim with this change was to add back correct and fast caching of the computation of the lower and upper wavelength limits of the spectral locus. However, there were a few other things about the API of the `ObserverData` regarding the access of spectral locus values as well that has been an itch for me when learning and using this library. So I checked if I could improve on it in ways that I would find easy to understand and ergonomical to use. I hope you'll like it and that we can find some nice improved API that we both like :blush: 

Sadly it all went into one pretty big commit. It was really hard to make one change without making the others. But I'll explain each change here:

* Make `spectral_locus_index_min`, `spectral_locus_index_max` and `spectral_locus_by_index` private. Was there any use case I was not aware of that could prove these useful to a library consumer? To me it just felt confusing to expose this functionality both in the form of by-wavelength and by-index. The API surface became large, and these methods felt like internal implementation details. I moved them to the end of the `impl` body, since it's customary to keep public methods at the top where they are easier to find.
* Replace `spectral_locus_nm_min` and `spectral_locus_nm_max` with a single `spectral_locus_wavelength_range` that return both values as a typed range. It felt both more idiomatic and ergonomical to me to use the existing standard library type for expressing ranges. In almost all places this was used, it was used as `nm_min..=nm_max` anyway, so just passing the single range is simpler.
* Introduce caching of the spectral locus wavelength range back into the library! :tada: 
* Rename `spectral_locus_by_nm` to `xyz_at_wavelength` and relax the constraints on the allowed wavelength range. I think this new name fits better together with the sibling methods `xyz_from_spectrum` and others. I also did not see the need to limit the allowed wavelength. With good enough documentation the user will still be able to use it correctly. This allows sampling the entire range of the color matching functions. This data was previously hidden in this library and I wanted to find some way to expose it for users with special needs (for example rendering the full color matching functions as a graph)

I'm excited to hear what you think about these changes. If needed we can make adjustments and adopt only a subset of the changes.

author: htyu
body:
Introducing `tlx.local_alloc` which can be used to allocate a number of shared memory buffers.

For example, to allocate `NUM_BUFFERS` number of `float16` buffers, each has `BLOCK_MxBLOCK_K` shape:

  `  buffers = tlx.local_alloc((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K), tl.float16, NUM_BUFFERS)`

where `BLOCK_M`, `BLOCK_K`, `NUM_BUFFERS` are all of `tl.constexpr` type.

The op will be translated to the following-like TTGIR op:

`    %0 = "ttg.local_alloc"() : () -> !ttg.memdesc<4x128x128xf16, #shared, #smem> 
`

For now users have no control of specifying the swizzling mode for the buffers. The compiler will automatically figure that out based on how they are consumed, in a separate PR.

Fixes #421.

Then use `bevy run web` on a project with a custom web folder, including other files in that folder. Check that these files are served correctly.

You can also test `bevy run web --bundle`, but that was already working for me on latest `main`.

author: m-nash
body:
Reviving https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/pull/45715

API Proposal: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/115664

Add the ability to inject a proxy implementation for reading and writing a model type.  This will replace the default implementation that lives on the model itself allowing a caller external to the library to adjust how things are written in some advanced scenarios.

Specific service need is AOAI wants the ability to control which properties of the OAI models it shares are serialized when sending to azure service.  To do this they need to replace that implementation with their own custom implementation: 
> As part of a streaming chat completions request, users can add the `stream_options` property to the request body and set its `include_usage` property to `true`. This results in the service streaming back the number of tokens that were used as part of this request as an additional chunk before finishing the SSE response. OpenAI added the `stream_options` property for backwards compatibility reasons (in other words, instead of turning it on by default, users have to opt in). In practice, however, there is no reason for a user ever wanting to turn this off. Thus, in the OpenAI library (which is still in preview), we don't expose this property at all and always set it on behalf of the user. The issue then arises because Azure OpenAI does not support this feature yet and would fail if we were to send it in a request. We need a way for the Azure OpenAI library to prevent this property from being serialized.

To fix the issue, we need to ensure that the constructed file path is safe and does not allow access to files outside the intended directory. This can be achieved by:

1. Normalizing the path using `path.resolve` to remove any `..` segments.
2. Using `fs.realpathSync` to resolve symbolic links.
3. Verifying that the resolved path starts with the intended root directory (in this case, `process.cwd()`).

If the resolved path does not start with the root directory, the request should be rejected with an appropriate HTTP status code (e.g., 403 Forbidden).

find . -type f | grep "\.c$" | xargs sed -i 's/[ \t]\+$//'

Jira: PHOENIX-7610

For the range scan or point lookup on the single row, it is required to provide either full pk columns with equal comparison (point lookup) or prefix pk columns with equal comparison operator (range scan).

However, when we use SQL CAST() function on pk columns to convert the type of the given column into another data type, the plan generated by where optimizer always performs full table scan instead of range scan or point lookup.

author: crobert-1
body:
<!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue.
Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.-->
#### Description
By definition, the [unmaintained status](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/component-stability.md#unmaintained) means that the component "does not have an active code owner." This PR moves code owners of two components (the `kinetica` and `opensearch` exporters) to emeritus.

`exporter/kinetica`: @TylerHelmuth was listed as the active code owner, but [moved the exporter to unmaintained](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/36808).

`exporter/opensearch`: This component was marked unmaintained as a part of https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/35781. It looks like there's an effort to add new code owners (which is great to see), but that does not include @Aneurysm9, the user currently listed as the code owner.

_This PR also adds the `seeking_new: true` flag to all unmaintained components as per the [documentation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/component-stability.md#unmaintained), "Components that are unmaintained are actively seeking contributors to become code owners."._

The reason for this change is the listed code owners in component READMEs do not match the `.github/CODEOWNERS` file. This is because the build tool generating the CODEOWNERS file [does not check for code owners of unmaintained components](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-build-tools/blob/6bdbad9c2432ef2c34105a2c65357ffa2d86666d/githubgen/codeowners.go#L48). This follows the definition of unmaintained so I believe we should follow the definition here rather than modify the build tool.

_Credit to @pjanotti for pointing out this discrepancy_

author: a-stewart
body:
If you have a button which includes an icon but no text, it still has the 3px margin - which results in the button being off centre

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e3861b4-2466-4f69-8fbd-fa244eac9635)

This change updates the CSS to only apply that 3px margin if there is slotted content.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2060298-ee5c-4edd-b596-b504817f1f50)

As such for regular buttons this should be a noop, but for buttons which only specify an icon, it should correctly centre the icon in the button.

---

It also applies a height 100%, since if there is no content, this can also cause the button to get vertically squished if it is placed in a flex with other buttons.

author: markrickert
body:
## Description

This makes a few changes to @fpena's expo 53 branch in #2938:

1. Updates to the tsconfig. All these changes bring our config in line with [the expo sdk 53 config](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/packages/expo/tsconfig.base.json).
  * `moduleResolution` changed from `'node` to `bundler`
  * `module` changed from `es2015` to `preserve`
  * Added `"customConditions": ["react-native"]` to the compiler options.
2. These updates to the tsconfig revealed some issues that weren't caught by the `yarn compile` command previously. Mostly just accidentally substituting `ViewStyle` for `TextStyle` in the type declarations.
3. Fixes the maestro tests so the same flow works for all permutations of `expo/non-expo + newArch/oldArch`. ... simplifies the number of files/scripts needed, and reduces the amount of logic needed to bypass both the dev server picker screen and the dev menu bottom sheet from expo that shows up in expo dev builds in the oldArch.
4. updates some packages to the correct versions that `npx expo install --fix` told me to update including the `@types/react` and `expo-router` deps.
5. During the course of updating packages, i moved the eslint config for the main ignite package to a javascript file and made it inherit from the boilerplate's config so that our linter is consistent throughout.

# Overview
This PR is about #189 and #190 .

cc. @NurAycaIlhan , @zeynepyaman 

# Screenshots
## Before the Changes
The visuals of the product manager page before this PR (everything is static besides the drawer menu and the log out button):

The "Comment Moderation" section:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70228cfe-337a-4be7-ae94-bd3d2152a64c)
