## Delivery Management
The filter that offers 4 options for the `deliveries` table, which shows "All" by default:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1630756-4d46-4af2-a9fc-f35f691fd3d3)

Only "Pending":

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b6070d5-4cff-47eb-8338-6a8d5a03c8aa)

Only "Shipped":

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bb223a9-1022-4c42-92dc-ea461284eb17)

Only "Delivered":

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53e4c56e-be93-4864-b1cb-7ac58cf1e9ed)

### Note
As you can see, if the delivery status progresses, the buttons the product manager can click get disabled.

## Example for Buttons and Changing Delivery Status
### Shipping
Let's go with this example, where I already know:

```sql
SELECT
    d.delivery_id,
    d.order_id,
    o.user_id,
    d.shipped_date,
    o.order_date,
    d.delivery_status,
    o.status AS order_status,
    d.tracking_number
FROM
    deliveries d
JOIN
    orders o ON d.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE
    o.order_id = 23;
```

That:

```
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
| delivery_id | order_id | user_id | shipped_date        | order_date          | delivery_status | order_status | tracking_number     |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
|          18 |       23 |      46 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | pending         | processing   | TRK-20250513T211042 |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
```

And on the webpage:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da4d8f14-a8cc-4694-b8fe-2cd160cc01f1)

So let's try to ship it. Here's what the table for this exact item looks like:

```
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
| delivery_id | order_id | user_id | shipped_date        | order_date          | delivery_status | order_status | tracking_number     |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
|          18 |       23 |      46 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | pending         | processing   | TRK-20250513T211042 |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)
```

And after clicking the blue "SHIP" button, the database correctly gets updated to:

```
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
| delivery_id | order_id | user_id | shipped_date        | order_date          | delivery_status | order_status | tracking_number     |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
|          18 |       23 |      46 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | shipped         | in-transit   | TRK-20250513T211042 |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)
```

And we can verify this by checking the "Shipped" deliveries:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40b001a5-a5c9-4eaa-9adc-f1b2cc3d3699)

And if the customer checks their profile page, they'll see:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a12c3ad9-f519-48de-b129-cf41513614f6)

Or more specifically:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14763a16-3c42-4c88-a1fb-ce2522338aaa)

### Delivering
Now let's try to click the green "DELIVER" button. I'll use the same example as the continuation, so `order_id=23, delivery_id=18` basically.

So if I click the button now:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82aa5c96-0260-485f-8f04-95351a00a907)

And the database gets updated correctly:

```
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
| delivery_id | order_id | user_id | shipped_date        | order_date          | delivery_status | order_status | tracking_number     |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
|          18 |       23 |      46 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | 2025-05-14 00:10:42 | delivered       | delivered    | TRK-20250513T211042 |
+-------------+----------+---------+---------------------+---------------------+-----------------+--------------+---------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)
```

As it can also be seen on the delivery management system:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49c21734-cd45-47d1-bbc5-110786743a24)

> Look at the last item with Order ID 23, it says `Status: delivered`.

And finally, the customer will see:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfb01428-9e09-42cc-8102-66070ff61627)

So this feature fully works now.

author: adhusson
body: `floor(id)` is the largest `totalAssets` that would max the relative cap of the id at its current allocation. We maintain a tree that counts the floors of ids that have a relative cap < WAD and an allocation is > 0. Floors are bucketed to make the tree small (see picture). `bucket(floor) ~ log_1.011(floor)`. We keep a counter of the number of floors in each bucket. Conservative: if `index(totalAssets) == maxNonEmptyBucket`, revert. ---- Specific to version B: * tick precision: 1.1% * max 255 ids per bucket. If the max is reached, you must allocate differently or change the cap. Important: when all relative caps are maxed, they all have the same bucket, which is the bucket of the current total assets. So you can't have > 255 maxed ids. * ids with floors above `type(uint128).max` all go in the largest bucket, so they are always considered maxed. This is OK since such an idea would be maxed by all `totalAssets <= type(uint128).max`.

author: abtink
body:
This commit adds the `OTBR_BORDER_AGENT_MESHCOP_SERVICE` CMake option, which maps to the `OTBR_ENABLE_BORDER_AGENT_MESHCOP_SERVICE` macro.

This new configuration controls whether the OTBR platform's `BorderAgent` module publishes the `_meshcop._udp` mDNS service (including the ePSKc service). It can be used to disable platform layer service registration so to enable/allow OpenThread core's Border Agent module to handle this responsibility.

This configuration is enabled by default. It is explicitly disabled in GitHub workflows, specifically in `border_router.yml`, where OpenThread core mDNS/DNS-SD support (along with use of the native SRP advertising proxy) is enabled.

author: taylorwilsdon
body:
## Pull Request Description (Markdown-only)

### Summary

This PR **centralises Google Workspace OAuth configuration and unifies authentication** across Calendar, Drive, and Gmail tools.
Key benefits:

* Single source-of-truth for scopes and redirect-state mapping
* Less duplicated helper code
* Cleaner README examples and credential path (`.credentials/you@example.com.json`)

---

### Key Changes

* **Config**

  * New `config/google_config.py` contains all scope constants, the combined `SCOPES`, and `OAUTH_STATE_TO_SESSION_ID_MAP`.

* **Auth Layer**

  * `auth/google_auth.py`

    * Adds `CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRETS_PATH` auto-detection.
    * Replaces `start_auth_flow` with an **async** version returning `types.CallToolResult`.
    * Drops hard-coded `DEFAULT_REDIRECT_URI`; value is now passed from the server.

* **Server**

  * Removes local scope constants; now imports everything from `config/google_config`.
  * Uses the shared `CONFIG_CLIENT_SECRETS_PATH`.

* **Calendar / Drive / Gmail Tools**

  * All tools call the new `start_auth_flow` directly and delete their bespoke `_initiate_*_auth_*` helpers or decorators.
  * Drive tools support `DRIVE_FILE_SCOPE` and optional `mime_type`.
  * Calendar tools add helper to normalise `timeMin` / `timeMax` to RFC 3339 UTC.

* **README**

  * Updates credential-storage path and `get_credentials` usage example.

* **Logging / DX**

  * Consistent log messages and clearer error handling.

---

### Breaking Changes

1. Scope constants now live in `config/google_config.py`; update any downstream imports.
2. Decorator-based auth helpers are removed—use `await start_auth_flow(...)` instead.
3. `start_auth_flow` is **async** and its signature requires `service_name` and `redirect_uri`.

---

### Changelog (Keep a Changelog style)

#### Added

* `config/google_config.py`
* Async `start_auth_flow` with richer guidance messaging

#### Changed

* README authentication examples and credential path
* All tools/server import scopes from the new config
* Drive `create_drive_file` now supports `mime_type` and uses `DRIVE_FILE_SCOPE`

#### Removed

* `auth/auth_flow.py` decorator and per-tool `_initiate_*_auth_*` helpers

---

Please double-check downstream imports and ensure any third-party callers await the async `start_auth_flow`.
